doc.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Playing on Ricky Nelson's first record
summary: Smith recalls the rock session in the late 1950s where Ozzie Nelson said he did not understand it but it was selling.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: That’s great. Well I want to thank you for your time today.
This was a really eye opening experience. By the way do you remember the tune that you played with Ricky Nelson that one session?
No. It was, I hate to tell you how long ago that was.
Yeah. That was like the very beginning of his career as a teen idol though.

Middle to late 50s in there you know. It was one of the early — it wasn’t a really radical thing, it was just that it had that rock thing with only four chords and the guitar and the spang-a-lang and the whining and all that routine. And Ozzie was A&Ring in the booth and he made that statement, you know he said, “now you know how I felt when I heard your first arrangement.” He said, “I don’t know what the kid’s doing but apparently it’s selling.”
